Subject: ISV Collab Prospectus: FluxForge Connect + Redwood Runtime

Hi Elena —

Hope you’re well. FluxForge’s work on developer tooling for LLMs has been on our radar; I think there’s a clear product fit between FluxForge Connect and Redwood’s serving/runtime capabilities. In particular we see three initial integration areas that could unlock joint GTM and product value:

- LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK adapters so customers can route calls to their FluxForge pipelines through Redwood’s hosted and dedicated runtimes
- Tracing & attribution hooks (trace headers, token attribution) so customers keep observability across SDK -> runtime -> model
- A prebuilt sample that demonstrates cost-aware routing + fallback to lightweight quantized variants for bursty workloads

I attached a short product brief and a draft mutual action plan to kick off the conversation. If this sounds interesting, could we do a 30–45 min sync next week to map ownership and milestones? I’m available Tue/Wed mornings (PDT) or Thu afternoon.

Next steps I propose if we align: sign the attached NDA, finalize MAP, and scope a technical spike (2–4 weeks) with an engineering liaison on each side.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context and the MAP. Quick technical readout and an initial delivery plan from engineering:

Summary (TL;DR)
- Feasible. We can deliver the three integration slices in a staged approach. No infra blockers for hosted/Dedicated; for Private/VPC we’ll need a short network checklist.

Proposed phased spike (2–4 weeks)
Week 0 (kickoff / environment): NDA + access provisioning; define sample customer scenario and test prompts; exchange minimal network and IAM requirements.
Week 1 (adapter spike): Implement a LangChain connector that converts LangChain call stacks to Redwood API calls; validate token attribution headers and basic streaming. Deliverable: adapter repo and smoke test.
Week 2 (tracing + KV/attribution): Add trace headers and token attribution metadata (opt-in); prototype prefix/KV caching hooks to ensure alignment with Redwood’s prefix caching APIs; deliverable: trace events in our dev observability pipeline.
Week 3 (sample & performance): Build the cost-aware routing demo that demonstrates fallback to a quantized variant vs standard model and measure latency/cost delta at small scale. Deliverable: demo app + MAP updated with metrics.

Dependencies / asks from FluxForge
- A dev account on FluxForge Connect with a sample pipeline and a test API key for staging
- Any SDK surface area docs (LangChain/LLamaIndex adapter expectations) 
- Security point-of-contact to answer specific questionnaire items (we’ll respond with SOC 2 snapshot and data flow diagram)

Risks & mitigation
- If FluxForge requires end-to-end customer tracing with PII in traces, we’ll need to define redaction/PII-handling rules up front — we will not ship PII in traces by default.
- For Private deployments we’ll need an approved network allowlist and a small on-prem checklist; this may add 1–2 weeks.

Estimate: 3–4 engineer-weeks for the spike (two engineers part-time over 3 weeks) + product & PM coordination. If spike is successful, pilot scoping (customer-facing) is +6–8 weeks.

Next steps I’ll take: upload a brief SOW template and a draft MAP with realistic milestones to the shared link, and prepare the SOC 2 snapshot we can share under NDA. Vanessa, can you confirm whether FluxForge prefers a paid POC or co-marketing-first approach?

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Software Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference
